chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'Those who join what Allah has Bidden to be joined.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your relatives.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'join what Allah has Bidden to be joined' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise exegetical report from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic phrase 'those who join what Allah has Bidden to be joined' as specifically referring to maintaining ties of kinship (*silat al-rahim*). This narration underscores the theological weight of familial bonds in Shia jurisprudence, linking general divine obedience to the specific social duty of preserving family relations, a concept central to the chapter's theme of goodly relationship with relatives.
